subsystems.name: Scoop coil
subsystems.role: generates the magnetic field that deflects and funnels the stellar-wind plasma.
parts: superconducting cable wound into a large loop

subsystems.name: Plasma funnel and braking region
subsystems.role: the magnetic geometry where incoming plasma is turned, compressed and slowed.
parts: plasma injector to inflate the magnetosphere

subsystems.name: Energy conversion
subsystems.role: turns the plasma's kinetic and thermal energy into electricity.

subsystems.name: Collection and separation
subsystems.role: condenses the captured gas and splits hydrogen from helium.

subsystems.name: Cryogenic storage
subsystems.role: holds propellant and fusion fuel as liquid or solid.

subsystems.name: Station-keeping and structure
subsystems.role: keeps the collector in the right place and orientation without a propellant-hungry tug.

buildSteps.title: Pick the collecting orbit
buildSteps.detail: Choose a heliocentric orbit near 1 AU, where the wind is densest, or a position such as a Sun-Earth Lagrange point. There is no useful wind in low Earth orbit, where the planet's magnetosphere shields it.

buildSteps.title: Size the field against the wind
buildSteps.detail: Balance the wind's ram pressure — at 1 AU only a few nanopascals — against the coil's magnetic pressure. Because a dipole field falls off with the cube of distance, the loop must be tens to hundreds of kilometres across, or the field must be inflated by injected plasma.

buildSteps.title: Design the coil
buildSteps.detail: Wind high-temperature superconducting tape into a loop carrying a large current, compute the hoop forces on the frame, and work out the cryogenic load that must be radiated away.

buildSteps.title: Assemble in space
buildSteps.detail: No rocket can launch a multi-kilometre loop, so it would be built from many small modules, inflated and rigidised, or spun up to hold its shape.

buildSteps.title: Magnetise and inflate the magnetosphere
buildSteps.detail: Energise the coil, then inject a small amount of plasma so the plasma carries and enlarges the field, creating a magnetic bubble far wider than the hardware — the magnetoplasma-sail idea.

buildSteps.title: Brake the plasma and extract charge
buildSteps.detail: A static magnetic field only deflects charged particles — the Lorentz force does no work on them. Energy must be taken out where plasma crosses field lines: an MHD channel with electrodes and a load, or an oscillating field that induces currents in the flow.

buildSteps.title: Capture and separate the gas
buildSteps.detail: The slowed plasma recombines at the collector, and the resulting hydrogen and helium are cryopumped, then distilled to enrich the helium-3 fraction.

buildSteps.title: Store or ship the product
buildSteps.detail: Liquefy and store the propellant, or transfer it to outbound vehicles as reaction mass.

buildSteps.title: Demonstrate and scale
buildSteps.detail: Fly progressively larger loops, measuring how much plasma is actually caught — grams first, tonnes only much later if ever.

prerequisites.why: high-temperature superconducting tape and space cryocoolers exist, but no coil larger than a few metres has flown.
the scoop's diameter sets how much wind it can reach, and nothing that large has been assembled in orbit.
MHD generators have been run in ground test facilities, but never in a tenuous space plasma.
studied in simulations and vacuum-chamber plasma tests, with no flight demonstration of useful collection.

prerequisites.tech: Cryogenic gas separation and storage at scale
prerequisites.why: separating and storing hydrogen and helium in space for years has not been done at these volumes.

pathway.milestone: paper studies of interstellar ramjets and magnetic sails, plus lab plasma experiments; solar-wind spacecraft measure the resource in situ
pathway.unlocks: a quantified picture of how thin and fast the wind is.

pathway.milestone: a small superconducting loop flown in space, showing that it creates a measurable magnetic bubble and drag
pathway.unlocks: proof that a scoop field behaves as modelled.

pathway.milestone: a magnetoplasma collector that captures recoverable grams of plasma over months
pathway.unlocks: real numbers on collection rate, mass and power balance.

pathway.milestone: a propellant depot that refuels spacecraft from harvested solar-wind gas
pathway.unlocks: a supply of reaction mass and hydrogen away from Earth.
a niche fuel source, though the energy caught remains a tiny fraction of what a solar array of the same area would produce.
